messages:
alex_ryan: Quick heads-up — premerge throughput audit for the v2.2 runtime kernel change showed a ~12% throughput regression on short sequences (<=64). Running in staging canary now, filing this thread for async triage and a go/no-go.

maria.k: can you paste the raw numbers + what workload?

alex_ryan: workload: chat-small (avg tokens 22). run: `./bench --profile chat-small --seed canary-v2.2`

```
Throughput summary (tokens/s)
baseline v2.1: 9800
candidate v2.2: 8600
delta: -12.2%

p50 latency: +4ms
p95 latency: +9ms
kv-hit-rate: 0.87 -> 0.85
```

alex_ryan: test was single-device A100, batch sizes auto, continuous batching enabled. Not huge latency spike but throughput hit is consistent across 3 runs.

devon: hm. any change to batching or packing code in that PR? I reviewed the kernel selection bit but not batching heuristics.

alex_ryan: PR touched kernel choice and a tiny change to the eager-padding heuristic. suspect interaction with small sequence path.

samir: can we repro with `--no-batching` to isolate?

alex_ryan: good idea, running now. will DM logs.

ci-bot: CI job 2874 completed — perf-matrix: chat-small: baseline 9800, candidate 9700 (+1%), long-seq: baseline 4000, candidate 4100 (+2%).

maria.k: CI numbers look less bad — maybe staging env differs (KV cache warmup or colocated daemons). alex, did you warm the KV cache between runs?

alex_ryan: I did cold-start then 3 steady-run iterations; warmup helped a bit but steady-state still shows ~8-10% gap.

devon: if it's only short sequences, could be packing. Try: 1) disable eager-padding, 2) force kernel A vs B, 3) capture flamegraph of token loop.

alex_ryan: running variants now. attaching quick flamegraph link: https://perf.internal/fg/1918765432 (will expire in 24h)

samir: I scanned flamegraph — candidate shows extra time in `pack_and_pad()` in the small-path. Looks like we added a memcpy in the new kernel chooser.

alex_ryan: aha — the memcpy was introduced to align buffers for a new fused kernel. we can make it conditional.

ops-oncall: decision needed for tomorrow's rollout to prod canary. what's proposed mitigation?

devon: two options: 1) hotfix to avoid memcpy on short seqs (low-risk), or 2) restrict canary traffic to 5% and add fallback route to v2.1 for chat-small routes. Prefer 1 if we can turn around fast.

maria.k: do we have tests to prevent regressions like this? suggest adding a microbenchmark to CI that asserts throughput delta < 3% for short-seq profile.

alex_ryan: I can open the hotfix PR in ~90m. If we can't ship before the scheduled canary, prefer option 2 (limit + fallback).

devon: +1 for hotfix. If PR ready in 90m and bench passes in staging, we can keep rollout. If not, ops-oncall please gate canary.

ops-oncall: acknowledged. I'll hold the prod canary at deploy-time unless CI shows candidate v2.2 microbench pass for chat-small. If no signal by T+2h, we'll restrict to 5% and enable route fallback.

samir: I'll add the microbenchmark to perf-matrix CI job (fast check) — will post results here when green.

alex_ryan: thanks everyone — will update in this thread. planning to include the conditional memcpy guard + unit test.

ci-bot: perf job queued (#2880) — microbench chat-small scheduled.

alex_ryan: quick note: if we do hotfix, let's also add a telemetry flag to surface memcpy hits per route for future triage.

maria.k: agreed. Adding that as a follow-up ticket.

devon: final call: if perf job passes (delta <= 2%) we approve canary rollforward. otherwise gate per ops-oncall plan.

ops-oncall: recorded. will act accordingly. :+1:
